description_full: Innovent Biologics, Inc., a biopharmaceutical company, engages in the research and development of antibody and protein medicine products in the People's Republic of China, the United States, Europe, and internationally. The company discovers, develops, manufactures, and commercializes monoclonal antibodies and other drugs for the treatment of oncology, ophthalmology, autoimmune, cardiovascular, and metabolic diseases. Its commercial stage product portfolio includes TYVYT (sintilimab injection), BYVASDA (bevacizumab injection), SULINNO (adalimumab injection), HALPRYZA (rituximab injection), PEMAZYRE (pemigatinib), olverembatinib, Cyramza (ramucirumab), Retsevmo (selpercatinib), FUCASO (Equecabtagene Autoleucel), SINTBILO (tafolecimab injection), DUPERT (fulzerasib), DOVBLERON (taletrectinib adipate), Jaypirca (pirtobrutinib), limertinib, SYCUME (teprotumumab N01 injection), mazdutide, PECONDLE (picankibart injection), and TABOSUN(Ipilimumab N01 injection). In addition, it sells and distributes pharmaceutical products; and offers consultation and research and development services. The company was incorporated in 2011 and is headquartered in Suzhou, the People's Republic of China.

financial_summary: Innovent Biologics Inc. is a large-cap healthcare business with a $19.3B market cap on $2.0B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +39% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +24.4pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at -5% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 83% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $1.4B in free cash flow — roughly 71 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 12.29× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 27× is fortress-like.

Net dilution runs at 3.7% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insiders hold 6.2% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 1.9× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
